facts.claim: Scheduled Emmy Kernel IR to PTX through guarded GPU transformations, typed LLVM IR, and LLVM NVPTX.
facts.qualification: LLVM supplies optimization and code generation; Deuteron is a scheduled-IR backend, not a general graph compiler.

facts.claim: 27 documented pass, analysis, policy, and lowering entries.
facts.qualification: Counts the 27 source-linked rows in the Compiler passes inventory, including lowering mechanisms and analyses. LLVM internal passes are separate; this is not a claim of 27 independent pass modules.
entry_names: Blocked recurrence loads and address hoisting

facts.claim: 15 open workloads spanning pointwise operations, reductions, matrix multiplication, normalization, and attention.
facts.qualification: Coverage and performance claims are limited to this open set.

facts.claim: 270 balanced-order RTX 5090 warm measurement calls; every call passes its original output checks.
facts.qualification: Total includes Deuteron, generated CUDA/NVCC, and the tested Triton baseline. All six compiler order permutations per workload are retained.

facts.claim: Equal-weight geometric mean of warm kernel latency: 3.752 us Deuteron, 6.216 us generated CUDA/NVCC, 4.332 us tested Triton.
facts.qualification: Computed from each workload/compiler median across six recorded calls. Excludes compilation, assembly, transport, and application overhead.

facts.claim: 1.66x versus generated CUDA/NVCC and 1.15x versus this Triton baseline on the 15 open workloads.
facts.calculation: baseline geometric mean latency divided by Deuteron geometric mean latency
facts.qualification: These are workload-set warm latency ratios, not a comparison with cuBLAS or every tuned Triton implementation, and not a claim of end-to-end speedup.

facts.claim: 103 of 103 public tests pass on Python 3.13 with H100 CUDA tests and assembly enabled; no skips.
facts.qualification: The suite includes CPU interface, cache, parser, and runtime tests; this is not 103 distinct GPU workloads.

facts.claim: All 11 native SM120 feature examples pass on RTX 5090.
facts.qualification: These are correctness examples, separate from the 15-workload performance comparison.

facts.claim: BF16x3 and TF32x3 tensor products with FP32 buffers and accumulation; packed BF16 fragments can use ldmatrix.
facts.qualification: BF16/TF32 are internal operand formats. Three high/residual products omit the low-by-low term and approximate FP32 multiplication under the tested tolerances.

facts.claim: Global-to-shared cp.async copies of 4, 8, or 16 bytes, with commit/wait groups and barriers.
facts.qualification: The TF32x3 demo retains the asynchronous copy ring. TMA, WGMMA, and TMEM are not implemented.

facts.claim: FP16 scalar/vector global storage with exact widening, nearest-even narrowing, and explicitly typed FP32 arithmetic.
facts.qualification: The supported pointwise subset has no native half arithmetic, half shared/tensor path, or public BF16 buffer transport. Converted NaN payloads are unspecified.

facts.claim: Structural transforms preserve original launch geometry, buffers, inputs, and tolerance contracts when their guards accept.
facts.qualification: Unsupported features fail explicitly; validation does not prove arbitrary IR bounds, synchronization, termination, or universal IEEE behavior.

demo.scope: CPU-only compile and inspection of actual emitted instructions; no assembly, GPU run, timing measurement, or new numerical-correctness claim.

presentation_caveats: Say 27 documented pass/lowering entries, not 27 independent compiler passes.
Say 103 public tests with H100/assembly enabled, not 103 GPU workloads.
Label performance as RTX 5090 warm kernel latency over the 15 open workloads.
Name the LLVM NVPTX backend and the tested NVCC/Triton baselines explicitly.
The demo proves compilation and instruction emission; its performance and GPU correctness are not measured during this capture.
LLVM supplies optimization/code generation; eligibility under the hackathon's prohibition on existing compilers remains unconfirmed (SUBMISSION.md).
